summary: 13 candidate substrates (Research, Epistemic, Nomenclature, Representation, Observation, Experiment, Evidence, Provenance, Transformation, Perturbation, Projection, Discovery, Meta) and a 7-stage ladder (State, Transition, Temporal History, Transition Topology, Computational Structure, Representation, Meta-Substrate).

limitation: O-0 mixes two different kinds of thing: substrates of the object of study (representation, transformation, perturbation, projection, observation) and substrates of the research process (epistemic, evidence, discovery, nomenclature, provenance, experiment). Several O-0 substrates share one formal type: perturbation, projection, encoding and observation are all maps on state spaces or on dynamics.
alternatives: B: two levels (object / meta) with typed maps
C: drop 'substrate' vocabulary entirely and use established terms only
rationale: B removes duplication (one typed Map concept instead of three substrates) while keeping the object/meta split explicit; C was rejected for now because the umbrella terms are useful as directory-level organisation, with formal statements using established terms.
migration: Every O-0 name is mapped to an O-1 location in research/ONTOLOGY.md; no O-0 name is deleted. The 7-stage ladder is kept as an investigative ladder and demoted from structure to hypothesis H-003.
note: Motivated by conceptual analysis at bootstrap (R1), before any experiment. Later evidence bearing on it is recorded in ontology_history as it arrives.

summary: Object level: Representation, Dynamics, Maps (typed: encoding, decoding, abstraction/projection, observation, perturbation, structural perturbation, refinement, compilation), Observation (= map + recording mechanism + clock). Meta level: Epistemic (statuses, hypotheses, evidence, discoveries, failures), Nomenclature, Provenance & Continuity (experiments, runs, research states). Meta-Substrate: open question OP-002, not a substrate.
